title: Reliability of Topic Modeling
task: Quantifying reliability of topic models across random replications
problem: The de facto reliability check (share of topics matched across runs at cosine > 0.7) ignores document-topic variation and has no statistical grounding.
architecture: Applies measurement-theory reliability coefficients to replicated topic models: Cronbach's alpha, maximal reliability and McDonald's omega (via factor analysis of each topic's document distribution across replications), including a multivariate omega; compared with the standard topic-matching practice.
baselines: standard practice (Maier et al. topic matching)
key_results: On trivial synthetic data the standard practice reports perfect reliability while alpha, maximal reliability and omega reveal the variation.
CFPB with LDA: multivariate omega 0.92283 (20 topics), 0.82235 (50), 0.74957 (100); downstream accuracy ranges 0.67-0.81 across replications at 20 topics.
strengths: Grounds topic-model reliability in established psychometric theory; code released.
Shows downstream conclusions vary with model reliability.

limitations.text: Existing reliability measures assume linear errors; only LDA (and STM) studied; comparison against a single baseline method.
